# Artificial paleomagnetic data for the tutorial

Thermal demagnetization data of 71 oriented drill-core specimens from 10 sites, used by
`09_apsg_paleomag.ipynb` and the paleomagnetism section of `apsg_tour.ipynb`.

**The data are artificial.** They were generated by `scripts/make_pmdata.py` of the repository (fixed random seed, so
the result is reproducible). Site and specimen names, the location and every number are invented;
nothing here comes from a real study or a real locality. The generator follows the physics of a
paleomagnetic experiment so that the data look like a typical study:

- every site has its own bedding (dip direction 20-350, dip 18-60) and a characteristic
  remanence (ChRM, magnetite-like, unblocking between about 400 and 585 C) acquired *before* the
  tilting, normal at seven sites and reversed at three; site means scatter like secular variation;
- a soft overprint along the present field unblocks below about 300 C;
- three specimens of site PM04 and one of PM08 have overlapping unblocking spectra, so their
  demagnetization paths follow great circles; one specimen each of PM02, PM06 and PM09 has a
  scattered, poorly behaved remanence; three specimens were not heated to the end of the schedule;
- the cores have random azimuth and hade, the magnetization (log-normal intensity, instrument noise
  floor, ~1 % relative noise) is stored in specimen coordinates, and two heating schedules are used.

**Files**

| File | Content |
|----|----|
| `PM01.1a.pmd` ... `PM10.7a.pmd` | one specimen each, PMD format read by `Specimen.from_pmd` (`<site>.<number>a`) |
| `sites.csv` | site table: location of the (hypothetical) study, bedding, number of specimens |

The moments are given for a nominal volume of 1 cm3, so the PMD files hold the magnetization in
A/m as well. The directions in the Dg/Ig/Ds/Is columns are computed from the core orientation and
the bedding written to each file.
